Subject: Private control plane: SAML/SCIM & IAM questions

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're starting the security review for Redwood Private (VPC deployment) and have a few technical questions to confirm before procurement moves forward:

- SAML support: Do you support both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows? Can you provide sample SAML metadata (XML) for the control plane SP?
- Attribute mapping: Which required attributes do you expect in the assertion (email, uid, groups, role)? Any constraints on NameID or format?
- Provisioning: Do you support SCIM v2 for user/group provisioning? How is the SCIM endpoint exposed inside our VPC — must it be publicly reachable or can it be internal-only (PrivateLink / internal ALB)?
- IAM roles: For cross-account access to customer-managed storage or KMS, what role assumption patterns do you support? Are role ARNs required at deployment time?
- Token/certificate rotation: Recommended cadence for SCIM tokens and SAML certificate rotation?
- Audit/evidence: Can you provide a simple artifact that shows audit logs for control plane access (for our SOC evidence collection)?

If possible, please send configuration templates we can hand to our IdP (Okta) team. Happy to schedule a short call with our security and infra folks.

Regards,
Ivan Morozov
Head of Cloud Security, Acme Corporation

Subject: Re: Private control plane: SAML/SCIM & IAM questions

Hi Ivan — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (solutions) and Vivek (security/infra) to provide the detailed artifacts. Below are quick answers and I'll attach templates you can hand to Okta: saml_config_template.yaml and scim_provisioning_map.csv. (See attachments.)

Quick answers:
- SAML: We support both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated SSO. SP metadata (XML) is included in the saml_config_template; we accept both email and persistent NameID but recommend using email (urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress) for mapping. Groups are supported via eduPersonEntitlement or a groups attribute.
- SCIM: We support SCIM v2. SCIM endpoint can be deployed internal-only (reachable via PrivateLink or an internal ALB). For Private deployments we recommend mTLS between your provisioning runner and our SCIM endpoint for stronger authentication.
- IAM roles: We require the customer to create a passive role that Redwood can assume for specific integrations (S3, KMS). We will provide example IAM trust policy and least-privilege ARNs in the attached design doc. Role ARNs can be provided at deployment or during onboarding; tagging helps for rotation audit.
- Rotation & audit: We recommend rotating SCIM tokens every 90 days; SAML signing cert rotation every 12 months (or sooner). We provide audit logs for control plane auth events (login, token lifecycle, provisioning actions) and can export to your SIEM via a secure forwarder.

Next steps: 30-minute call with your IdP and infra to walk through metadata + a small test account (SCIM). Are you available tomorrow at 15:00 PT?

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Ivan, Rafael — adding the technical details and one recommended deployment pattern for the private control plane:

Recommended pattern (for AWS-hosted private control plane inside your VPC):
1) SAML/SP metadata: Deploy our control plane SP fronted by an internal ALB with a customer-managed certificate (ACM private CA or customer cert). SP endpoints are accessible inside the VPC. Provide us with your IdP metadata XML; we will provide the SP metadata back.
2) SCIM endpoint: Expose SCIM behind an internal ALB with mTLS. Our connector supports a short-lived bearer token (scim-provisioning-token) plus optional client cert verification. Endpoint URL should be reachable from your provisioning runner (e.g., a small EC2 or transient CI job inside the VPC). No public exposure required.
3) IAM role assumptions: Create an IAM role with a trust relationship that allows our deployment principal to assume the role (we provide the principal ARN). Minimal permissions example: s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject (prefix-scoped), kms:Decrypt for keys we need to access. Add condition-based restrictions (aws:SourceVpc, aws:SourceIp) where possible.
4) Attributes & claims: NameID=email, email, uid, groups (multivalued). For provisioning create a claim mapping of 'groups' -> SCIM groups; we recommend sending group membership claims for role population in the control plane.
5) Rotations: We support automated SAML cert baking — provide a rotation window and we will coordinate. SCIM bearer tokens should be rotated via your secrets manager; we recommend 90-day rotation with on-demand revoke capability.
6) Audit & evidence: For SOC requests we can provide an export: authentication_events.csv (timestamp, principal, action, IP, reason). We also publish per-route access logs to a customer-configurable S3 bucket (or push to your Splunk/Datadog).

Attachment: redwood-private-iam-design.pdf (detailed IAM examples, SAML metadata snippet, SCIM mapping examples).

Technical notes:
- For on-prem VPCs or air-gapped deployments, we can offer an out-of-band metadata exchange (signed XML over SFTP) and a local-only SCIM endpoint with a temporary test user seeded at install time.
- If you need SCIM delta-provisioning only, we can enable incremental syncs and avoid full re-imports.

Happy to present diagrams on the call.

—Vivek
Head of Infrastructure Security, Redwood Inference
